artists.biography:
Crippled Black Phoenix is a rock supergroup from the United Kingdom. Several musicians have contributed to Crippled Black Phoenix's albums and play with them during their live shows.

Members of the band used to play in other bands (including Iron Monkey, Gonga, Mogwai, Electric Wizard and others). In 2004, Justin Greaves began recording primitive sounds he had in mind for years. He was encouraged by Dominic Aitchison, and their ideas would lay the backbone for Crippled Black Phoenix.
Although originally having an unorthodox start, since all the band members were part of and busy with other projects at the time of the band's founding, Crippled Black Phoenix remained committed to staying together and forged their sound. The band writes what they call "endtime ballads," signifying both the slightly macabre nature of their songs and their unusual blend of styles as the final evolution in music. This blend has led to them being called everything from stoner-prog to freak-folk to doom.

Crippled Black Phoenix have made live shows a focus and have performed in unusual venues, using Victorian-era instruments in tandem with more modern instruments.

perplexity.description:
(Mankind) The Crafty Ape is a studio album by British progressive rock band Crippled Black Phoenix, released in 2011 on Mascot Records. The album represents a significant point in the band's career trajectory, arriving after their relocation to a new label and establishing their mature sound within the progressive rock landscape. The album's structure spans over 52 minutes across multiple chapters, with opening track "Nothing (We Are)" setting the tone for an expansive sonic journey that includes compositions such as "The Heart Of Every Country" and "Get Down And Live With It."

The album showcases Crippled Black Phoenix's command of complex arrangements and layered instrumentation characteristic of progressive rock, blending atmospheric passages with heavier instrumental sections. The band's approach on (Mankind) The Crafty Ape demonstrates their ability to construct lengthy, narrative-driven compositions that build emotional depth through careful dynamics and orchestration. This release solidified their position within the UK progressive rock scene and contributed to their growing reputation among genre enthusiasts.

The album was followed by the mini-album No Sadness Or Farewell in 2012, indicating a period of sustained creative output for the band. While specific critical reception details are limited in available documentation, the album's release through Cool Green Recordings and its substantial runtime suggest it was positioned as a major artistic statement within the band's catalog, appealing to dedicated progressive rock audiences seeking ambitious, compositionally intricate work.
